more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
No current country-wide food-use ban was confirmed in the regulatory sources checked in 2026.
The permissions checked in 2026 apply only to the specified preparations, food uses and conditions.
more_info.overview: Lycopene is a red carotenoid pigment; the specification covers synthetic material as well as preparations extracted from tomatoes or produced by fungal fermentation. It is used to add colour or restore colour lost during food manufacture. Specified lycopene preparations can be made by chemical synthesis, extracted from tomatoes, or produced by fermentation with Blakeslea trispora. The source depends on the preparation. The specified material is supplied as red powder or crystalline material. The specification describes it as effectively insoluble in water.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; flavoured drinks; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products; edible cheese rind.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.daily_intake: For lycopene: No ADI specified (JECFA, 2009). This evaluation does not establish an ADI for every form in the named group.
